name: peek-controls-close-the-card
description:
Peek controls, both looks: the /peekctl WebUI cluster next to a peek card renders its two buttons, carries the parent space's tint, and the close button really dismisses the card. Same fixture, gate and link coordinates as peek-dismiss-escape.json - a peek opened on this fixture, at this link, is a proven precondition, so this scenario reuses it rather than re-deriving it. Where it diverges: the dismiss comes from clicking .pkc-close on the controls widget's own document instead of the Escape accelerator, and the DOM/tint checks run against /peekctl (PeekControlsWidget::BuildContents, chrome/browser/ui/atrium/atrium_peek_widget.mm) rather than the card's own page. peek-controls.js's installPeekControls() renders one .pkc cluster holding two buttons, class pkc-close/pkc-popout plus the shared ov-btn class, each wired to chrome.send('peekControl', [kind]) on click. OnSurfaceMessage's 'close' branch calls owner_->RunDismissCallback(), the same funnel Escape uses (PeekWidget::OnEscapePressed), which is why the dismiss proof below is identical to peek-dismiss-escape's. The tint check expects '15 43 70' because oceanBlue (this fixture's space tint) resolves to #0F2B46 (rust/atrium-core/src/tint.rs) and PushOverlayTheme writes the RGB triplet as --atrium-space-tint on peekControlsReady - the same push command-bar-wears-the-space-tint.json already proved reaches a sibling overlay document.

ASSUMPTION FOR THE CONTROLLER: the ax_window_count assertion is written to expect the card AND the controls cluster both counted (one more than the 2-window baseline peek-auto-pinned/a sibling scenario measured for a plain peek-open state at min_area 200000), using a lower min_area (1000, comfortably under kPeekControlsSize's 70x38=2660 area) so the controls window is not floored out. But ax_window_count always reads LIVE state at the very end of the action list, after every action including the close click has already run, and the vm-scenario.sh runner has no way to sample it mid-run - so by the time this assertion's own retry loop (up to 8s) starts, the close IPC round-trip and the closing VLOG line have already landed, and the card's own 170ms dismiss animation (kPeekDismissDuration) may well have already finished too, since pulling the run log over SSH before assertions run is itself likely to take longer than 170ms. If this assertion is flaky or consistently reads back down to 1, that is this timing gap, not a widget bug - the controller should re-grade it against the close-button proof (the eval_equals checks and the theme_changed dim-region measurement below), which do not have this race.
